items.title: Earl Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002
items.q: Then Allen Smith was in another band... as a matter of fact we recorded that band. Richard Wyands on piano, Vernon on bass, I was on drums, Flip, Jerome and Alan.

ctx.x: And this is why he opened this? © Fillius Jazz Archive -21-

In 1955. In the middle of the year. So Benny Carter had the band there and one of our musicians here, Alan Smith, a very fine trumpet player who lives here, he was in the band. So they went down there and they opened up. Opening night after the gig they found Wardell out in the desert dead. So they don’t know whether it was a drug deal gone awry or — to this day nobody knows what happened. But that just has to do with Wardell Gray. And by that time I was working with Bob Scobey. And we were in Chicago at the Blue…
